accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a ballistic missile from a cruise missile?
o: A ballistic missile is powered throughout its flight, whereas a cruise missile is powered only during boost phase.
A ballistic missile follows a high parabolic trajectory after boost, whereas a cruise missile remains powered and generally flies at low altitude using aerodynamic lift.
A ballistic missile uses only aerodynamic lift, whereas a cruise missile follows a free-fall arc.
Both ballistic and cruise missiles follow the same powered, low-altitude trajectory.
accepted.x: A ballistic missile is powered mainly during the boost phase and subsequently follows a high parabolic or free-fall trajectory. A cruise missile is powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift while flying at relatively low altitude.
accepted.tq: Use the propulsion and flight-path contrast to separate the two missile classes.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nirbhay and Pralay — Air-launched missiles only
accepted.x: Agni and Prithvi are examples of ballistic missiles. BrahMos and Nirbhay are cruise missiles, while Pralay is classified as a ballistic missile in the given classification.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure missile-example pair and eliminate reversed classifications.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Hypersonic speed is generally defined as speed exceeding
accepted.x: Hypersonic flight refers to speeds greater than Mach 5.
accepted.tq: Identify the standard threshold associated with the technical term.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV):
1. It is initially rocket-boosted.
2. It subsequently glides and manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere.
3. Its manoeuvrability makes interception more difficult.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: An HGV is rocket-boosted before gliding and manoeuvring at hypersonic speed in the upper atmosphere. Its manoeuvrability and flight profile make interception difficult.
accepted.tq: Check whether all three statements describe successive stages and the resulting advantage.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: The HSTDV developed by India is primarily associated with which technology?
accepted.x: The Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV) is an indigenous scramjet demonstrator. SFDR, not HSTDV, is associated with solid fuel ducted ramjet technology.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related propulsion technologies by their exact programme names.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the HSTDV is correct?
o: It flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection above 2,000°C.
It flew at speeds below Mach 2 and tested only navigation systems.
It is a submarine-launched missile with a range of 3,500 km.
It is an air-defence interceptor tested only in the endo-atmospheric layer.
accepted.x: India's HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection at temperatures exceeding 2,000°C.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive speed and thermal-performance figures to identify the correct statement.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a scramjet?
o: A solid-fuel motor designed only for submarine-launched missiles.
A jet engine in which combustion occurs at subsonic speed after the air is completely stopped.
A propulsion system using supersonic combustion and having no rotating parts.
A rocket engine that carries all oxygen required for combustion.
accepted.x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and does not have rotating compressor or turbine parts. It is distinct from a rocket, which carries its oxidiser.
accepted.tq: Break the propulsion term into its defining combustion characteristic.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: The first flight-trial of India's long-range hypersonic missile was reported on
accepted.x: India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on 16 November 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate closely spaced test dates by linking each date to its specific programme.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile:
1. It is intended for the Navy's coastal batteries.
2. Its approximate range is 1,500 km or more.
3. It can attain a peak speed of about Mach 10.
4. It uses a two-stage solid motor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile is intended for naval coastal batteries, has a range of about 1,500 km or more, reaches up to Mach 10, and uses a two-stage solid motor.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of technical specifications, including range, speed, role and propulsion.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported flight characteristics of the long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile?
o: It uses skipping manoeuvres, with peak speed around Mach 10 and average speed around Mach 5.
It remains stationary in low orbit before descending vertically at Mach 3.
It flies only in a high parabolic arc, with average speed below Mach 2.
It uses underwater propulsion and approaches the target at subsonic speed.
accepted.x: The missile is reported to use skipping manoeuvres, with a peak speed of about Mach 10 and an average speed of about Mach 5.
accepted.tq: Use the peak-versus-average speed distinction to avoid reversing the figures.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology is intended mainly for
accepted.x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.
accepted.tq: Match the propulsion system with its stated operational application.

accepted.s: What is the principal feature of a Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) system?
o: Several missiles are permanently linked to one satellite for navigation.
A missile remains in a complete geostationary orbit before re-entry.
One warhead is divided into several non-explosive decoys only.
One missile carries several warheads capable of being directed towards different targets.
accepted.x: A MIRV allows one missile to carry multiple warheads, each capable of being directed at a different target.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and connect each term to its operational meaning.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Mission Divyastra is associated with the first test of MIRV technology on which missile?
accepted.x: MIRV technology was first tested on Agni-V under Mission Divyastra on 11 March 2024.
accepted.tq: Associate the named mission with the exact missile platform rather than the missile family generally.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best explains the Fractional Orbital Bombardment System (FOBS)?
o: A missile remains permanently in a complete orbit and cannot re-enter the atmosphere.
A warhead is placed into a partial orbit and can approach its target from an unexpected direction.
A cruise missile travels only through underwater channels before striking a target.
Several warheads are released from an aircraft without entering orbit.
accepted.x: In FOBS, the warhead enters a partial low orbit and can descend towards the target from an unexpected or different direction.
accepted.tq: Distinguish partial orbit from complete orbit and identify the direction-of-approach advantage.
accepted.sec: Missile classes and hypersonic technology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following speed classifications is correctly matched?
o: Nirbhay — subsonic; BrahMos — supersonic; BrahMos-II — hypersonic

Which of the following statements regarding the Arihant-class SSBNs is correct?
1. INS Arihant was associated with 2016.
2. INS Arighat was associated with 2024.
3. INS Aridhaman is the third boat in the sequence.
4. The platform is approximately 7,000 tonnes and can carry up to 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5 missiles.
